inputs.text: Wide cinematic frame, ultra-wide 2.4:1, the control hall of a vast starship in a stylized retro-futurist design: heavy rounded forms, brushed steel and cream ceramic panels, thick cable trunks, chunky analog-looking monitors and dials, 1970s science fiction. At the centre rises a colossal stepped pyramid of black and brushed-steel machinery covered with rows of glowing amber indicator lights, the Helm, a giant supercomputer brain. From its flat top a column of blue light projects straight up into the high ceiling, where it spreads into a faint hologram of thin rings. Around the pyramid stands a ring of tall monitor walls with amber and blue graphs and meters. Small figures of the crew in matching grey-olive coveralls with a yellow stripe on the shoulders sit at their consoles, seen from behind in shadow. In the foreground, seen from behind, stand two figures: a slender woman with short slicked-back blonde hair in a light grey uniform with yellow stripes on the shoulders and sleeves, and next to her a tall man in a long dark coat. Strong graphic shapes, limited palette of teal, amber, cream and black, painterly, slightly hazy, strictly no visible faces, no text, no logos.
